original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Does the orthogonal pair obtained by reflecting the pinned D6 anchors by one simple E8 root induce the same partner-support set after every coordinate permutation that carries the image pair back to the pinned pair?
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card asks for a new measured speedup. The revision-8 verification row says a published faster replay is not equivalent coverage until checked. Merged PR #6959 checked that coverage for one pinned D6 pair and left a reflected anchor pair open. This package transports that one simple reflection. It does not time an engine, rerun the pinned 2^20 census, or load the intersection-counter engine.
bottleneck_link: Deletion and decoder certificates reuse a low-weight iterator only if the equality survives a changed root list. This comparison binds the recorded D6 support set to one simple reflection of the pinned anchors. It does not change a supplier bill or kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after the eight-root coordinate-permutation census and the 466-vector weight-at-most-2 screen of simple root 3. Do not run the bit-lane iterator, walk the 2^20 kernel, screen the spinor complement, or transport a non-simple root.
evidence: Simple root 3, (0,-2,2,0,0,0,0,0), sends the pinned anchors to (2,0,2,0,0,0,0,0) and (2,0,-2,0,0,0,0,0). The reflected 30-line list has SHA256 bcc5dc15f642aca7bdcc1249d2588869b6510aa8e08cde8688fe340c665435b5. Its 15 matching frames have incidence rank 10. All 466 vectors of weight at most 2 were tested: the kernel words are zero and the 15 partner masks. All 40320 coordinate permutations were tested for each of the eight simple roots. Root 3 is the first that moves the pair and admits a coordinate permutation; exactly the 1440 permutations with {sigma(0), sigma(1)} = {0, 2} carry it, and each transports the partner masks onto 3, 24, 36, 768, 1152, 2112, 98304, 147456, 270336, 528384, 50331648, 75497472, 138412032, 270532608, 537919488. That list has SHA256 23a7b374a6bc62bc2aca47843d52a01fa8e791ed3a98085133829d816c5094e8. Simple root 0 moves the pair onto a spinor and has 0 carrying permutations; its absolute coordinates obstruct every signed coordinate permutation. A dropped support changes the hash.
author: unpaidmoon

open_questions.question: Does the image pair of simple root 0 have the same weight-at-most-2 set equality on its own 30-line complement?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That reflection also moves the pinned pair, and no coordinate permutation carries the image back. The support-hash comparison for root 3 does not answer the spinor complement.
open_questions.first_step: List the E8 lines orthogonal to (2, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) and (1, -1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, -1), and screen all 466 vectors of weight at most 2 against that frame code.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not build the spinor complement's frames.

open_questions.question: Does one coordinate root outside this simple system induce the same transported equality?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The eight simple roots are a complete census of this simple system only. A different coordinate root can move the anchors onto another axis pair.
open_questions.first_step: Transport the image of the E8 line (0, 2, 0, -2, 0, 0, 0, 0) by the coordinate permutations that carry it back, and compare the partner supports with hash 23a7b374a6bc62bc2aca47843d52a01fa8e791ed3a98085133829d816c5094e8.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package checks that the root moves the pair and does not transport the image.
